title: The Story of Janshah
summary: Prince Janshah, son of King Tayghamus of Kabul, was lost in the wilderness while pursuing an enchanted silver gazelle during a royal hunt...
full_text:
Prince Janshah, son of King Tayghamus of Kabul, was lost in the wilderness while pursuing an enchanted silver gazelle during a royal hunt. Wandering through mountains and valleys, he arrived at the Castle of the Flying Dames, situated beside an azure lake surrounded by weeping willows.

Every week, three magical doves of radiant white plumage flew down from the clouds, took off their feathery cloaks, and bathed in the crystal water as lovely maidens. The fairest among them was Princess Shamsah, daughter of the King of the Jinns of the Mountain of Jewels.

Janshah, captivated by her beauty, concealed her feather robe among the reeds. When her sisters took flight, Shamsah remained, and seeing Janshah’s noble countenance and respectful manners, consented to wed him and dwell in Kabul.

However, after several years, a thoughtless palace maid inadvertently revealed the hiding place of the feather robe. Shamsah donned the cloak, kissed her sleeping husband, and flew into the clouds, weeping: 'If you truly love me, Janshah, seek me at the Castle of the Mountain of Jewels!'

Janshah awoke to despair, but refused to surrender his love. He set forth on an epic quest across the world, passing through the Valley of Apes, traversing the Sea of Shadows, and winning the friendship of the King of Beasts through his justice.

A friendly giant eagle, moved by the prince’s unwavering fidelity, bore Janshah across the burning skies to the summit of the Mountain of Jewels.

There, before the court of the King of the Jinns, Janshah passed three trials of wisdom, courage, and discernment. The King of the Jinns blessed their union, and the royal lovers returned to Kabul, ruling in peace and enduring devotion.
moral: Perseverance in love, guided by courage and patience, conquers the most formidable enchantments.
